name: NCBI E-utilities
description: The programmatic door to every NCBI database - PubMed, PMC, GenBank, ClinVar, dbSNP and thirty more - through one small family of endpoints (esearch, efetch, esummary, elink). Old-fashioned and superbly documented, and still the canonical way to run a reproducible literature search.

license.name: US Government work; PubMed records are free to use

access.auth_note: works without a key at 3 requests/second; a free NCBI key raises it to 10/second
access.rate_limit: 3/second anonymous, 10/second with a key - exceeding it gets your IP blocked, not throttled
access.pagination: retstart and retmax; use the history server (usehistory=y) for large sets

recipes.title: Search then fetch, using the history server
recipes.code:
BASE=https://eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/entrez/eutils
curl -s "$BASE/esearch.fcgi?db=pubmed&term=sea+level+rise&usehistory=y&retmode=json" > s.json
QK=$(python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('s.json'))['esearchresult'];print(d['querykey'])")
WE=$(python3 -c "import json;d=json.load(open('s.json'))['esearchresult'];print(d['webenv'])")
curl -s "$BASE/efetch.fcgi?db=pubmed&query_key=$QK&WebEnv=$WE&retmax=20&rettype=medline&retmode=text" | head -20

gotchas.trap: Going over the rate limit gets the IP blocked rather than 429'd, and the block outlasts the run.
gotchas.fix: Sleep 0.34s between calls without a key, 0.1s with one, and always send tool= and email=.

gotchas.trap: efetch for PubMed returns XML even when you ask for retmode=json - only esearch and esummary speak JSON.
gotchas.fix: Parse XML for efetch, or use esummary if the summary fields are enough.
